title: Accounting Rule for Refundable Advances, Connection Refunds and Project Close-Out — Line Extensions and New Service Construction
content:
Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative accounts for the contribution on a **Line Extensions and New Service Construction** project, after energization, under the following rule.

## Rule

1. **Recording the advance.** Where the class's contribution class is a refundable advance, the whole contribution billed is recorded as an advance subject to refund.
2. **Earning refunds.** Each other permanent member who connects to the extension during the class's refund period, counted in months after the energized date, earns the project member a refund under the class's refund basis: a refund equal to the connecting member's own allowance, under that connecting member's own class of extension. Refunds earned in one year are paid in the class's refund payment month, January, of the following year.
3. **Ceiling.** Refunds are made until they reach the class's largest refundable share of the advance.
4. **Late connections.** A connection after the refund period earns nothing.
5. **End of the refund period.** At the end of the refund period the unrefunded advance is forfeited, becoming a nonrefundable contribution, and the project is closed.
6. **Nonrefundable projects.** A nonrefundable project is closed after energization.
7. **Payee.** Refunds go to the member who paid the advance and are never assigned to a later owner of the land.

## What counts as a connection

The connections counted are the permanent service accounts of other members energized on the extension built by the project, from the energized date through the end of the refund period. Each connecting service account earns one refund, and the refund is recorded with that connecting service account as its reference.

## Worked example (hypothetical Irrigation Well Extension, advance $20,000.00, refunds up to 100 percent)

| Connection within the refund period | Connecting member's own allowance | Refund earned | Refunds to date | Paid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Neighbor A, connected in September of year 1 | $4,425.00 | $4,425.00 | $4,425.00 | January of year 2 |
| Neighbor B, connected in May of year 3 | $12,000.00 | $12,000.00 | $16,425.00 | January of year 4 |
| Neighbor C, connected in August of year 4 | $7,500.00 | $3,575.00 | $20,000.00 | January of year 5 |

Neighbor C's own allowance is $7,500.00, but refunds stop on reaching 100 percent of the $20,000.00 advance, so $3,575.00 is earned. Had Neighbor C never connected, $3,575.00 of the advance would remain unrefunded at the end of the refund period; it would then be forfeited and the project closed. A neighbor connecting after the refund period earns the project member nothing.

## Payee illustration (hypothetical)

A hypothetical member pays a refundable advance on a pivot extension and later sells the land. Refunds earned by connections during the refund period are paid to that member, not to the buyer of the land.
